chunks: Hadith 3134 — Zur‘ah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

When you come to al-Mawqif, face the House and glorify Allah, the Exalted, one hundred times, and magnify Allah, the Exalted, one hundred times, and say: “Mā shā’a Allah, lā quwwata illā billāh” one hundred times; and say: “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, having no partner. To Him belongs the kingdom and to Him belongs all praise. He gives life and causes death, and causes death and gives life. In His hand is the good, and He is powerful over all things” one hundred times.
Then recite ten verses from the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqarah, then recite “Qul huwa Allahu Aḥad” three times, and recite Āyat al-Kursī until you finish it, then recite the verse of subjugation.
“Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself over the Throne; He covers the night with the day, which pursues it swiftly” to the end of it.
Then recite “Qul a‘ūdhu bi-Rabbi al-falaq” and “Qul a‘ūdhu bi-Rabbi al-nās” until you finish both of them.

Then praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for every blessing with which He has blessed you, and mention His blessings one by one, as much of them as you can enumerate; and praise Him for what He has bestowed upon you of family or wealth; and praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for what He has tried you with; and say: “O Allah, to You belongs praise for Your blessings which cannot be counted by number and cannot be repaid by deed.”

And praise Him with every verse in which He mentioned praise for Himself in the Qur’an; and glorify Him with every glorification by which He mentioned Himself in the Qur’an; and magnify Him with every magnification by which He magnified Himself in the Qur’an; and declare His oneness with every declaration of oneness by which He declared Himself in the Qur’an.

And invoke blessings upon Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and do so abundantly and strive in it; and call upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by every name with which He named Himself in the Qur’an, and by every name that you know well, and call upon Him by His names that are at the end of al-Ḥashr, and say:

I ask You, O Allah, O Raḥmān, by every name that belongs to You; and I ask You by Your strength, Your power, and Your might, and by all that Your knowledge encompasses, and by Your gathering and by all Your pillars, and by the right of Your Messenger, may Your blessings be upon him and his family, and by Your greatest, greatest Name, and by Your mighty Name by which whoever calls upon You, it is incumbent from You to answer him; and by Your most great, most great, most great Name by which whoever calls upon You, it is incumbent from You not to turn him away and to give him what he asks, that You forgive me all my sins within all Your knowledge concerning me.

And ask Allah, the Exalted, for all your needs from the matter of the Hereafter and the world, and express longing to Him for the visitation in the future and in every year; and ask Allah for Paradise seventy times, and repent to Him seventy times.

And let this be among your supplication: “O Allah, free me from the Fire, and expand for me from Your lawful and good provision, and ward away from me the evil of the wicked of the jinn and humankind, and the evil of the wicked of the Arabs and the non-Arabs.”
If this supplication is finished and the sun has not yet set, then repeat it from its beginning to its end, and do not grow weary of supplication, humble entreaty, and asking.

key_terms.آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ: the celebrated Qur’anic verse recited here as part of the devotional program
key_terms.النَّارِ: the Fire, from which the supplicant seeks deliverance
key_terms.الْبَيْتَ: the Ka‘bah, which one faces during this supplication
key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Paradise, which the supplicant asks Allah for repeatedly
key_terms.الْمَوْقِفَ: the standing place at ‘Arafāt during hajj
key_terms.رِزْقِكَ الْحَلَالِ الطَّيِّبِ: lawful and wholesome provision asked from Allah
key_terms.نَعْمَائِكَ: Your blessings and favors bestowed by Allah

ai.seo_question: What supplication and recitations are recommended at al-Mawqif in ‘Arafāt according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines a detailed supplication and devotional program for al-Mawqif at ‘Arafāt, combining dhikr, Qur’an recitation, praise, salat upon Muḥammad and Āl Muḥammad, and personal du‘a. It emphasizes gratitude for blessings, seeking forgiveness, invoking Allah by His names, and persisting in supplication until sunset.
